title: Symmetry-aware generative design of flat-band materials beyond known crystal-net prototypes
authors: Yihao Wei, Ivan Savochkin, Artem Mishchenko, Xiangwen Wang, Qian Yang
abstract: Flat electronic bands underlie a range of strongly correlated and topological phenomena, whose design in real materials has so far relied on a small catalogue of named geometric motifs such as kagome, Lieb, and pyrochlore nets. This discrete catalogue is by no means to exhaust the geometries that support flat bands in real compounds, as band flatness is a property of network connectivity. Here we combine a continuous geometric representation of crystal sublattices, with a symmetry-constrained generative model, to access a broader design space for materials hosting flat bands. The key step is to choose sublattice motifs that are outside the known geometric clusters, ensuring the novelty of the generated structures. We then introduce SkeleGen, which pins these unconventional skeletons to symmetry-compatible Wyckoff positions while denoising the surrounding chemistry, resulting in 9,352 crystal candidates that survive stability and flatnessscreening. Band flatness is confirmed using high throughput full DFT calculations, which agree well also with the tight-binding spectra of the isolated skeletons, supporting a geometric origin of the band flatness. We demonstrate "out-of-distribution" motifs as a new design principle to dramatically expand geometric repertoire for materials discovery, potentially beyond flat bands.
summary: This work introduces SkeleGen, a novel computational framework that overcomes the limitations of cataloged crystal motifs by treating flat-band connectivity as a continuous geometric property. By using symmetry-aware generative models guided by latent space analysis, the authors successfully designed and screened thousands of chemically plausible materials predicted to host exotic flat electronic bands.
main_problem: The design of flat electronic bands for strongly correlated and topological phenomena is limited by a small, known catalogue of geometric crystal motifs.
main_result: The authors developed SkeleGen to generate 9,352 novel, stable crystal candidates that retain the desired flat-band character traceable to unconventional sublattices.
method: A symmetry-aware generative model (SkeleGen) combines continuous geometric representation with structural constraints derived from Graph Neural Networks trained on sublattice embeddings.
model_or_system: The focus is on electronic band structure arising from specific lattice connectivity patterns, modeled by identifying and embedding 'flat-band skeletons' within larger crystal structures. Validation involves high-throughput DFT calculations.
key_observables: Band flatness (dispersionless bands), Novelty score ($	ext{S}_{	ext{novelty}}$), Flatness score ($S_{	ext{total}}$).
important_parameters: DFT calculation parameters (PBEsol functional, PAW potentials); Latent space thresholds (e.g., 50th percentile for novelty).
main_assumptions: The electronic properties are primarily determined by the connectivity of the underlying sublattice skeleton, allowing a geometric design principle to guide material discovery.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow: mapping known vs. unexplored latent space regions (UMAP), detailing the four-step constrained generation pipeline (SkeleGen), and showing representative candidates with their derived band structures.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression from identifying the limitation of existing motifs to developing a continuous geometric representation via GNNs, generating novel skeletons using SkeleGen under symmetry constraints, and finally validating these generated structures through high-throughput DFT calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the methodology—using generative AI (diffusion/GNN) constrained by fundamental physical symmetries to explore vast chemical spaces—is highly relevant for designing quantum materials with specific electronic properties.
